title: Allow plus removal in rename cleaner
summary: Allow punctuation-only rename cleaner terms, including '+', to match inside title tokens so staged custom negative terms can remove separators such as S03+SP.
reason: The backend matcher wrapped every custom term in alphanumeric boundaries. That made a symbol-only term like '+' fail when it appeared between alphanumeric characters, even after the operator staged '+' as a custom negative rename term.
behavior_before: Adding '+' to RenameMovieRemoveTerms or the WebView custom negative terms field did not remove the plus sign from names such as S03+SP because the generated regex required non-alphanumeric neighbors.
behavior_after: Symbol-only custom rename terms are treated as literal punctuation matches without alphanumeric boundaries, while word-like terms still keep boundary protection.
manual_validation: apps/desktop/runtime/Python/python.exe -c "from mediapipeline.core.rename.movie import clean_pipeline_movie_name; print(clean_pipeline_movie_name('Ascendance of a Bookworm S03+SP 1080p Dual Audio BD Remux FLAC-TTGA.mkv', remove_terms=['sp','+'], movie_filter_terms={'video_source':['bd'], 'release_groups':['ttga']}))" - returned Ascendance of a Bookworm S03
rollback_plan: Revert the movie_filter_term_pattern punctuation-only branch and remove the S03+SP regression test, then rerun the focused rename and Local API clean-preview tests.
notes: No filesystem mutation, rename apply execution, FFmpeg/media policy, subtitle conversion, audio routing, source/scratch/output movement, or pending-publish behavior changed. The touched rename files already contained unrelated uncommitted language/sub-dub filter changes before this packet; those changes were left intact.
